title: Shard-aware admission and soft-priority reclamation to reduce pool tail depletion
creator: Maya Singh
description: After the Jan 2025 capacity exhaustion incident that manifested as long tail latency and aggressive tenant throttling, we observed that admission decisions were being made at a coarse pool level and failed to account for shard-local headroom. This ticket designs and implements a shard-aware admission scoring layer plus a soft-priority reclamation mechanism to prevent pool-wide queue amplification and reduce emergency throttling events.
incident_summary: On 2025-01-29 hosted API experienced a GPU pool exhaustion event where sustained allocations from a small set of tenants caused queuing and hard throttling across the entire pool. The autoscaler recovered capacity slowly and runtime backpressure led to widespread 503s and elevated latencies for latency-sensitive customers.
detection: Detected by runtime SLO alerts (p99 latency and queue length) and spike in 503 rates. Pager duty triggered at 2025-01-29 03:12 UTC. Console dashboards showed multiple shards at >95% token-processing time with uneven utilization across shards.
root_cause: Admission control computed fairness scores at the pool level, not per-shard. A dominant tenant's long-running requests occupied a subset of shards, causing localized saturation and global admission counters to under-report local contention. Autoscaler reacted to average pool metrics, which delayed scale-ups while local shards were starved.
proposed_design: 1) Add shard-aware admission scoring: admission should combine tenant credit with shard headroom metrics (free_slots, inflight_estimate) so requests are routed to shards with capacity and scored accordingly. 2) Implement soft-priority reclamation: when local shard headroom drops below threshold, mark low-priority tasks eligible for non-disruptive preemption or graceful deferral with a short backoff. 3) Introduce per-shard emergency hints to autoscaler: expose a high-frequency signal to prime scale-up for affected shards. 4) Tenant-slice isolation experiments: allow pinning high-throughput tenants to bounded slices to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification.
acceptance_criteria: Admission scoring includes per-shard headroom and prevents admitting new requests to shards below threshold
Soft-priority reclamation can defer or gracefully preempt <5% of in-flight low-priority work during stress without data loss
Autoscaler receives per-shard emergency_hint metric with <5s latency and uses it to trigger proactive priming
Integration tests that simulate hotspot tenant show p99 latency improvement >=30% versus baseline
No regression in normal traffic: throughput variation <2% in steady-state

progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with infra, autoscaler, and SRE. Agreed on signals and initial thresholds.
2025-02-18: Initial ShardAdmissionScore prototype merged behind feature flag (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342). Unit tests added.
2025-02-21: SoftPriorityReclaim design doc shared in Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/shard-reclaim). Feedback from PM: prefer deferral with exponential jitter over forced eviction.
2025-02-24: Simulation harness updated with a 95th-percentile hotspot scenario; preliminary runs show 22% p99 improvement.
2025-03-01: Autoscaler hook implementation 60% complete; gating on high-frequency metrics transport optimization to avoid noise.
2025-03-01: Feature flag rollout plan drafted; canary cohort selection criteria defined.
review_feedback: PM (Aisha Patel): Ensure tenant notifications exist when requests are deferred so clients can implement retry jitter.
Security (Jin Park): Confirm no sensitive tenant metadata is exposed in shard emergency signals; suggested hashing tenant id in metrics.
Performance (Liam O'Connor): Benchmark suggests reclaim overhead <1% CPU; re-run with larger batch sizes to validate.
SRE (Noah Lin): Add clear abort conditions for canary to rollback automatically if p99 increases or error budget burns.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Reclamation may introduce request latencies for low-priority tenants - Mitigation: limit rate and provide explicit client-visible error codes for deferral
Risk: Per-shard signals increase metrics cardinality - Mitigation: aggregate signals at minute granularity and sample high-frequency traces only during canary
Risk: Autoscaler priming could cause thrash - Mitigation: add hysteresis and minimum priming interval
test_plan: Unit tests for ShardAdmissionScore boundary conditions and scoring behavior
Integration test: end-to-end loadgen injecting hotspot tenant and asserting p99 latency improvement
Chaos test: simulate delayed autoscaler reaction and verify soft-reclaim prevents full pool exhaustion
Canary: staged rollout to dev -> non-prod hosted pool -> small percentage of prod pools
rollback_plan: If canary increases p99 latency or error rates beyond thresholds, immediately disable shard-aware admission feature flag and revert autoscaler priming hook, then follow pool recovery runbook (drain shards and re-balance).
notes: This approach prefers graceful deferral over hard eviction to preserve inference correctness and avoid silent request drops.
Feature will be controlled by a runtime feature flag and an org-level policy to allow enterprise customers to opt-out of soft-reclaim behavior.
Follow-on work may include tenant-slice autoscaling where high-throughput tenants get reserved micro-pools.
